title: Agentic Systems Engineering: Loops, Context and Harnesses
tagline: Build an agent as a model in a loop calling typed tools, with most of the engineering in the harness
audience: Python developers and engineers. Day 1 starts from what a language model is and how it differs from ChatGPT, so no prior LLM, API or agent framework experience is needed.
prerequisites: Any laptop CPU with uv, or Google Colab. All model calls go to free API models (an OpenRouter key; a one-time 10-credit top-up raises the free quota from 50 to 1,000 requests a day). Node.js 22.19+ is optional, for the Pi teardown. Run 00_setup_check before Day 1; see labs/README.md.

outcomes.text: Implement a tool-calling agent loop without a framework, with typed tool schemas, a step budget and explicit completion criteria, given three synthetic port services and ten tasks
outcomes.evidence: a loop that completes at least seven tasks, with a trace per run

outcomes.text: Apply compaction, offloading of tool results and staged loading of skills, and measure the effect on tokens and success, given long tasks that overflow a fixed context budget
outcomes.evidence: a before-and-after table of tokens, cost and success

outcomes.text: Implement a protocol server over a document store and connect the agent to it through capability discovery, given the port's circulars and a provided test client
outcomes.evidence: a server that passes the provided tests, with a trace of discovery and calls

outcomes.text: Design a checkpointed state-graph agent with a human approval gate at a defined risk threshold, given booking changes, some of which affect safety or fees
outcomes.evidence: a graph that pauses, resumes after approval and survives a restart, with a test per path

outcomes.text: Evaluate the agent over repeated trials, including runs against a seeded prompt injection, given 20 tasks with five trials each and a circular carrying planted instructions
outcomes.evidence: success in every and in any trial, cost per completed task, and a logged injection run in which exfiltration fails

outcomes.text: Deliver the agent as a traced API service gated by a smoke evaluation in continuous integration, given a repository with a pipeline and a trace collector
outcomes.evidence: a run that passes on the baseline and fails on a seeded regression, and a README stating tools, permissions and operating limits

case_study.name: Marsa Ports Authority
case_study.summary: Marsa Ports Authority is a fictional Red Sea port authority with three services: a berth schedule, bilingual tariff circulars and a booking service with write actions. Participants build Bosla, its booking assistant, as a model in a loop calling typed tools: the loop from scratch, a context budget, a context file, a tariff skill and an MCP server over the circulars, an SDK comparison, a check of every booking against the schedule, evaluation over repeated trials, a booking graph that pauses for the duty harbour master at a risk threshold, an injection attack and its containment, and an API service gated in CI. All data is synthetic and generated with a fixed seed.

capstone.summary: An individual project: build a working agent system on one of three tracks and submit it as a public GitHub repository before the Day 5 deadline. AI coding assistants are allowed for the code, but you own every design decision, number and claim. There is no live demo and no presentation: the README is the presentation, backed by saved evidence of real runs (eval CSVs for both configurations, plus logs or traces, a transcript, screenshots or a short recording). Rafeeq in production: the Madar assistant as a complete service with MCP tools, memory, approvals, security, evals and an API; Your harness: a domain harness for a real workflow in your entity, with context files, permissions, a loop and evals; Graph workflow: a durable, human-in-the-loop process as a graph with agents inside nodes. Minimum: 3+ tools (one over MCP), a context file plus memory or retrieval plus a compaction or budget rule, an approval on a write action with step and cost budgets, 15+ eval tasks on two configurations with an error analysis, and a security note (trifecta, one attack, one defence), using synthetic or public data only. Starter kit: labs/capstone/.
